impact: silencieux

reponse: 'FALSE'

::: {.piege}
```{r}
0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3
```
:::

## Why

R stores decimal numbers in binary, in the IEEE 754 format. Just as 1/3 has no finite decimal expansion, most numbers like 0.1 have no finite binary one: R keeps an approximation. The sum of the two approximations is not exactly the approximation of 0.3, and `==` compares down to the last bit.

The pitfall hides in filters: `df[df$rate == 0.3, ]` can return zero rows without the slightest warning.

## The fix

Compare with a tolerance. `all.equal()` applies one by default, but returns a string when the values differ: wrap it in `isTRUE()`.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
isTRUE(all.equal(0.1 + 0.2, 0.3))
abs((0.1 + 0.2) - 0.3) < 1e-8
```
:::
